text_summary.body: On 27/XII of the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's captivity, Evil-merodach in his accession year released him, spoke kindly, set his throne above the other kings in Babylon, and gave him a daily allowance for life.

setting.body: Nebuchadnezzar died in early October 562; Amēl-Marduk's accession year ran to Nisan 561, so its twelfth month (Addaru) fell in Feb–Mar 561. Ration lists of Nebuchadnezzar's thirteenth year (592/1) already record oil for Ya'u-kīnu, king of Yahudu, and his sons at Babylon.

constraints.textual_assertion: Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign … in the twelfth month
assumptions: Accession year (from Oct 562); the twelfth month (Addaru) of that year falls in Feb–Mar 561 (Parker & Dubberstein table).

constraints.textual_assertion: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin

competing_reconstructions.label: 27th (2 Kgs 25:27) or 25th (Jer 52:31) of the twelfth month
competing_reconstructions.summary: A two-day difference between the parallel accounts.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik notes the release in the thirty-seventh year and quotes Wiseman that the Hebrew implies an agreement, not merely kind words.
